question: Which acid is predominantly present in tomatoes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxalic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxalic acid** is a dicarboxylic acid that is found in many plants, including tomatoes.
 
• It is a strong acid and can be harmful if ingested in large quantities.
 
• With the molecular formula C₂H₂O₄, oxalic acid is a dicarboxylic acid. It is also referred to as oxiric acid or ethanedioic acid.
 
• There are numerous plants and vegetables that contain this chemical component.
 
• With the condensed formula HOOC-COOH, it is the most basic dicarboxylic acid and has a more acidic nature than acetic acid.
 
• Other acids mentioned in the options are also present in tomatoes, but in smaller amounts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetic acid** is the main acid in vinegar and is also found in tomatoes, but in much lower concentrations than oxalic acid.
 
• **Carbonic acid **is formed when carbon dioxide dissolves in water and is not naturally present in tomatoes.
 
• **Tartaric acid **is found in grapes and is commonly used in winemaking.
